segments.text: Good evening. This is Aakashwani. I am Sahira Muchthaba with the news at 9.
The headlines
Prime Minister Narendra Modi says ongoing global crisis highlighted clean energy as
key to ensuring future energy and economic security. Says, country working towards 500
GW renewable energy target by 2030. Finance Minister Nirmala Sita Raman says, government
to continue prioritizing capital spending to maintain growth momentum while ensuring fiscal
discipline. Home Minister Mitch Shaw orders setting up our foreigners' regional registration
offices in all state capitals by next year. Sevilla Cyclonics Tom Morrisu likely to make
landfall near Angol in Andhra Pradesh between midnight and early hours tomorrow,
Andhra Pradesh and Orissa step up evacuation and disaster preparedness measures.
And in Youth Olympics games, Judo Ka Khushbu Darjada assures India of a medal by reaching
women's 63 kilo final in Senegal, then the Desengu becomes first Indian female swimmer
to qualify for the final.
And now the news in detail.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said, the ongoing global crisis have highlighted
that energy security was directly linked to economic security.
way. He emphasized that the future of energy and economic security lies in clean energy.
Mr. Modi was addressing the gathering after inaugurating the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit
Mr Modi said the global economy faced unprecedented crisis over the past few years, ranging from
the COVID-19 pandemic to the ongoing crisis in West Asia.
He said it is a matter of pride that India, with a population of 140 crore, effectively
navigated these global challenges while sustaining high economic growth.
He said the country was firmly progressing towards its target of achieving 500 gigawatts
of non-fossil fuel-based energy capacity by 2030.
The Prime Minister observed that the next phase of the solar revolution will depend not only
on wider adoption, but also on innovation.
He stressed the need to bring every government building, school, college, hospital and street
lighting system under solar power.
Speaking on the occasion, new and renewable energy minister Prahlad Joshi said, the sector
had attracted investments worth US$67 billion over the past two years.
In September 2024, India's non-fossil installed capacity crossed 200 gigawatts and today
it has gone beyond 310 gigawatt. This remarkable progress has been achieved in just two years
under the leadership of the Honourable Prime Minister."
The Prime Minister also visited various exhibition stalls and interacted with exhibitors. The
theme of the four-day summit is, Invest, Innovate, Inspire. It is witnessing participation
from more than 130 countries, including over 40 ministers. Finance Minister Nirmala
Sita Raman has said the government will continue to prioritise capital expenditure
to sustain India's growth momentum while ensuring fiscal discipline.
Ms. Sita Raman was speaking at a private event in Mumbai today.
She said capital expenditure had delivered good results over the past four to five years
through its multiplier effect and will remain an important part of the government's growth
strategy. She also identified credit access, insurance and pensions as priorities for the
phase of financial inclusion.
For the poorest of the poor who can't afford to pay premium, government comes in, subsidizes
the premium and makes them participate in insurance and in pension schemes. Insurance
for all by 2047 is already a goal for government of India. Insurance should deepen and go
to the last citizen who needs to get covered. And the credit without any doubt is a top
priority because we want credit access to everyone who wants to do some business or
expand access to business and so on.
Home Minister Mit Shah has directed that foreigners' regional registration offices,
FRROs, be established in all state capitals by next year. At present, FRRO offices are
operational in 20 states. According to the Home Ministry, the number of foreign nationals
visiting India for tourism, medical treatment and education has increased substantially,
creating the need to expand the FRRO network across the country.
The ministry said the central government is pursuing the establishment of FRROs in
the remaining nine states, i.e. Bihar, Guwah, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhupradesh,
Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Meghalaya.
More from our correspondent.
The establishment of these FRRO offices will help foreigners visiting India in
obtaining various consular services including visa extension, conversion, immigration compliance
and legal safety.
The expansion will strengthen local-level institutional capacity, improve coordination with estate
authorities and facilitate legitimate foreign visitors.
The Foreigner's Regional Registration Office regulates, tracks and facilitates the lawful
estate of foreign nationals wasting or residing in India.
Overall, the FRRO monitors compliance with Indian immigration laws, handles cases
of off-arrest and visa violations, and coordinates legal action or penalty where
necessary.
Anand Kumar, Aakashwani News, Delhi.
Welcome back, you are listening to News at 9.
The severe cyclonic storm Urusu over the Bay of Bengal is very likely to cross the South
Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongol between midnight tonight and early hours tomorrow.
IMD Director-General Mritinjay Mohanpatra said,
the cyclone will cross Andhra Pradesh coast with wind speeds of 100-110 km per hour,
gusting up to 120 km per hour at the time of landfall, bringing heavy rainfall.
A severe cyclonic storm that developed over the Bay of Bengal
is gradually moving in the northwest direction.
The landfall process is expected to begin around midnight tonight and will be completed
by 4 a.m. tomorrow.
The cyclone is expected to cross the coast near Angol between Nellore and Narsapur.
The governments of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have stepped up evacuation efforts and disaster-preparedness
measures to deal with the cyclone.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandra Babu Naidu has directed all government departments
to remain on high alert and take necessary precautionary measures to minimize the loss of
life and damage to property. More from Abba Correspondent.
of ambulances. Electricity restoration teams, equipment and additional personnel from Chennai
are being deployed. Officials have been directed to safeguard tanks and reservoirs, prevent
flooding and restore essential services within 48 hours. Fishermen have been advised not
to venture into the sea, while people are urged to stay indoors and follow official
warnings.
In Odisha, around 1,50,000 people have been evacuated from vulnerable areas and shifted
to shelters and other safer locations.
The fresh weather threat comes at a time when several parts of southern Odisha are still
struggling to recover from the impact of cyclone or nub.
Our correspondent has the details.
Southern Odisha is once again facing a serious weather challenge due to severe cyclonics
from Murasu, particularly in Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandamal, Raigada, Korapot, Malkangiri and
Kalahandi.
Around 150,000 people have been evacuated to cyclone shelters and other safer locations.
NDRF and ODRAF teams along with fire services personnel have been deployed in vulnerable
areas to undertake rescue and relief operations.
Schools in vulnerable districts will remain closed tomorrow and the day after.
With the resin steel struggling to recover from cyclone Arnab and the devastating
targeting floods, Murasu poses another major challenge for the state administration. The
cause thus for Akashwari News, Bhuvaneswar.
Ahead of the festival of Diwali, which falls on the 8th of this month, the Supreme Court
has permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers in Delhi and India during specified
hours on 7th and 8th of November. The apex court further ordered that the complete
ban on firecrackers in Delhi and India imposed earlier will come back into force
from 9 November.
The Commission for Air Quality Management, CAQM, has invoked all measures under Stage
2 of the Graded Response Action Plan, or GRAP, with immediate effect across the entire
national capital region.
The decision was taken after Delhi's Air Quality Index, or AQI, was recorded at 324
today, placing it in the very poor category.
Under Stage 2 of GRAP, concerned agencies have been directed to intensify mechanical
and vacuum-based road sweeping along with regular water sprinkling and use of dust suppressants.
The measures also include increasing parking charges to discourage the use of private vehicles.
The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation has announced that it will operate 20 additional train
trips on weekdays from tomorrow following the implementation of Grab 2 in Delhi.
You are listening to News on 9 on Akash Mane.
Welcome back.
The Bharati Ajanta Party conducted a Lokantra Bachao-Arajyakta-Hattao foot march campaign
across the country to counter protest and allegations of the opposition parties.
As part of the campaign, senior BJP leader Amit Shah addressed a massive public rally
in Hyderabad. He strongly criticized the Congress party over its recent political rallies, accusing
it of attempting to protect illegal infiltrators rather than creating genuine awareness about
voter rights. Mr. Shah asserted that no illegal infiltrator would be allowed to exercise
voting rights. The Jharkhand unit of the BJP also launched its Loktantar Bacha Rajakta
Hatafut March campaign in Ranchi.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of Pune metro
projects worth around 21,800 crore rupees tomorrow afternoon through video conferencing.
These projects will strengthen Pune's public transportation infrastructure and improve
connectivity across the city.
Indian judoka Khushbu Raja Kabhai Darjada has assured the country of at least a medal
at the Youth Olympic Games at Dakar in Senegal.
15-year-old Khushbu entered the final of the women's 63-kilogram category after defeating
Algeria's Dhonia Berahal. She will now face Germany's Hohena Reinholt, the reigning cadet
world champion in the gold medal match later tonight. Meanwhile, Dhinidhi Desinghu has
created history by becoming the first Indian female swimmer to qualify for the Youth Olympics
final after advancing to women's 100-meter freestyle medal race.
In Men's Hockey Asian Champions Trophy into a defeated South Korea 8-0 in the final league
stage match at Jalan Thirindpanjab, in the first match of the day, China and Bangladesh
played out a one-all draw in the second match, Japan defeated Malaysia by 2-1. From Wednesday,
the semi-final stage will begin.
Benchmark domestic equity indices surged nearly 1.7% today, extending their rally
for the third consecutive session. The sensex soared 1,233 points to close at 75,693.
In our bilingual live phone-in program, PublicSpeak, tonight at 9.30pm, we will bring an insightful
discussion on Keth Bachao Abhiyan and the future of sustainable agriculture with Dr.
Rajashree Roy Burman, Assistant Director General, Agriculture Extension ICAR. During
the program listeners can ask questions on the subject to participate simply dial
telephone numbers 01123310481930 PM onwards.
And now, before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Prime Minister Modi says ongoing global crisis highlighted clean energy as key to
ensuring future energy and economic security, says country working towards 500
gigawatt renewable energy target by 2030. Finance Minister Nirmala Sita Raman says
as government to continue prioritizing capital spending to maintain growth momentum while
ensuring fiscal discipline.
Home Minister Mitra order setting up of FRROs in all-state capitals by next year.
Severe cyclonic storm Urusu likely to make landfall near Angol in Nandapradish between
midnight and early hours tomorrow.
And in Youth Olympics Games, Judo Ka Khushbu Dharjada assures India of a medal by reaching
